title: Adani Enterprises Plans Rs 35,000-40,000 Crore Annual Capex Over Next Two Years
excerpt: Airports, data centres and the Mundra PVC complex will lead Adani Enterprises' Rs 35,000-40,000 crore annual capex, after record first-half EBITDA of Rs 11,958 crore.
body:
• Adani Enterprises plans capital expenditure of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore a year over the next couple of years, its head of finance said on the earnings call.
  • Airports, data centres and the Mundra PVC complex will do "the heavy lifting", Manan Vakharia said.
  • The guidance follows record first-half FY27 EBITDA of Rs 11,958 crore, up 56 per cent, on consolidated income of Rs 71,569 crore, up 62 per cent.
  • For investors, management gave no specific EBITDA forecast for FY27 — the next signals are PVC commissioning in the next financial year, data-centre capacity rising toward 500 MW, and the Navi Mumbai airport ramp.

Adani Enterprises Ltd plans to spend between Rs 35,000 crore and Rs 40,000 crore annually over the next couple of years, with airports, data centres and its proposed PVC complex emerging as the biggest investment drivers, the company said during its earnings call, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

"We expect to do capex at a run rate of around Rs 40,000 crore. So, we may be somewhere in the range of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore, which is the rate we expect to continue over the next couple of years."

— Manan Vakharia, Head of Finance, Adani Enterprises

"The heavy lifting will be done by airports, data centres and PVC," Vakharia said. The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, while bringing its large manufacturing investments closer to commercial operation.

What was reported

Adani Enterprises, the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, reported its highest-ever half-year EBITDA of Rs 11,958 crore for the six months ended September 2026, an increase of 56 per cent from a year earlier. Consolidated income rose 62 per cent to Rs 71,569 crore, while profit before tax from continuing operations increased 45 per cent to Rs 3,297 crore, the BusinessLine report said.

Chief Executive Officer Arun Bansal said the company was progressively moving from a "build-out phase to value realisation phase", as investments made over the past few years begin contributing more meaningfully to earnings.

Where the money goes

The airport business and data centres are central to that transition. Adani Airport Holdings reported a 52 per cent increase in first-half EBITDA to Rs 3,275 crore. In the September quarter, the airport portfolio handled 21.3 million passengers, revenue rose 20 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,786 crore, and EBITDA increased 55 per cent to Rs 1,641 crore, with non-aeronautical revenue growing 57 per cent. The portfolio comprises eight airports, including Navi Mumbai International Airport, and accounts for about 23 per cent of India's passenger traffic and 29 per cent of its air cargo volumes, according to company officials. Navi Mumbai began international operations on July 15, and management expects it to reach its full annual capacity of 20 million passengers by the end of FY28.

AdaniConneX, the data-centre joint venture, has expanded its contracted capacity to more than 1.2 gigawatts and signed a new 240-megawatt hyperscale contract during the September quarter. Operational capacity stood at 94.6 MW after handing over an additional 29.2 MW to customers. The company expects operational capacity to reach 120-150 MW by the end of the current financial year and approach 500 MW over the following 12-18 months. Of 1.4 GW under development, 1.2 GW has already been tied up, management said.

The other major investment is a 1-million-tonne-per-annum PVC manufacturing complex at Mundra, Gujarat, involving capital expenditure of about Rs 26,000 crore. Around 60 per cent of project spending and construction has been completed, and the first part is expected to be commissioned in the next financial year. The facility will also include related chemicals and chlor-alkali operations.

Separately, the company has completed expansion of its solar module manufacturing capacity to 10 GW and expects to commission 6 GW of solar cell capacity by the end of the current financial year. It sold 1,478 MW of solar modules in the September quarter, up 35 per cent from a year earlier, as reported by Urban Acres' summary of the call.

What to watch next

The guidance is an annual run-rate expectation, not reported performance — actual spending will depend on project schedules and execution. Management did not provide a specific EBITDA forecast for FY27. For readers following the stock, the tests are therefore operational: whether the first PVC commissioning lands in the next financial year, whether live data-centre megawatts move toward the 500 MW mark, and whether Navi Mumbai and the wider airport portfolio keep converting passenger growth into earnings as the heavy capex continues.
